text:
Nadia R: Short follow-up from the allocator sync. Proposal: define a concise lease handshake so orch retains topology/safety and scaler handles short-lived prewarm/active leases. State idea: REQUESTED -> GRANTED -> PREWARM -> ACTIVE -> RELEASING. Orch node states: FREE, RESERVED, RETIRING.

Omar H: Sounds good. Two quick things: how do we encode urgency and how does orch communicate lack-of-headroom so scaler can fallback?

Nadia R: Add preempt_priority in RequestLease. Orch returns admission_status in {OK, THROTTLE, QUEUE_BURST, DENY} plus reason_code like "headroom_low". Scaler can then call fallback_model() or reduce_batch().

Priya S: Obs: include a lease_id and timestamps (req, grant, prewarm_done, active, release) so Console can map latency. Also emit decision_rationale short string for postmortems.

Claire V: Edge-case: draining while client still holds KV cache. Proposal: Release(lease_id, expected_release_ts) -> orch replies {ACK, ACK_GRACE_MS, FORCE_REVOKE}. FORCE_REVOKE emits kv_evict metric and a routed-fallback event. Enforce a tenant-level max_grace_ms.

Omar H: To avoid noisy scaling, add probe_cooldown_seconds per tenant (default 45s) and exponential backoff for failed prewarms. Also orch should reply with suggested_backoff_ms when it cannot grant.

Nadia R: Minimal RPC sketch: RequestLease(tenant_id,demand_est,preempt_priority) -> {status,lease_id,ttl_ms,admission_status,decision_rationale,assigned_node}; KeepAlive(lease_id)->{status,new_ttl_ms}; Release(lease_id,expected_release_ts)->{status,grace_ms}; OrchEvents(stream)-> {lease_granted,lease_revoked,headroom_update}.

Priya S: +1. Also tag grants with billing_tag for prewarm accounting.

orch-bot: autoscaler-dev: rollout of "lease-handshake" succeeded :white_check_mark:

Claire V: I'll add a tiny unit test that fuzzes simultaneous RequestLease calls. Omar, can you run a contested-headroom sim and measure fairness?

Omar H: Yup, I'll prototype a sim next week.

Nadia R: Thanks all — I'll draft a short RFC with the proto snippets and state diagram and share for review. Target: EOW. :thumbsup:
